analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts for the threat-review tooling (.github/scripts/test-threat-diagnostics.py and test-threat-model-review.py). They do not touch provider runtime, the coordinator WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, cache storage or any asset/boundary in the canonical model (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041 and others). No product code path changes.

In test-threat-diagnostics.py, the multi-tier integration test now stubs scanner.paid.plan_calls and asserts plans == [2, 1]. This is a test of call-budget planning only; there is no security-relevant behavior change.

In test-threat-model-review.py (head lines ~743-761), the workflow-boundary test tightens assertions about the workflow file. THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA must come only from github.event.pull_request.base.sha, with no env fallback, which strengthens pinning of the canonical threat model to the immutable PR base. The workflow timeout rises to 60 minutes with a 3000s scanner timeout. BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY=workload, BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS (default 500) and BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (default 16384) must be present, and the old BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_CALLS is forbidden. workflow_dispatch, pr_number and review_depth must be absent from the review job, which prevents manual or arbitrary-PR triggers on the secret-bearing pull_request_target workflow. These tests assert the existing controls: pull_request_target with the default-branch scanner checkout, no head.sha or head.ref use, persist-credentials false, and hash-pinned pip install before Bedrock credentials.

The workflow YAML itself is not in the supplied units, so I cannot verify that it matches these assertions. The cost and availability implications of a 500-call workload cap and a 60-minute timeout are outside the supplied evidence. Integration should confirm that the workflow and scanner changes (budget_scan, paid planner) are consistent with these tests.
